memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "One day he went into the house to attend to his duties, and none of the household servants was inside. She caught him by his cloak and said, 'Come to bed with me!' But he left his cloak in her hand and ran out of the house." - Gen 39:11-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The moment finally comes when the temptation is at its most intense. Joseph is alone in the house, no one else around — the perfect opportunity to sin unseen. Potiphar's wife physically grabs his cloak and demands, "Come to bed with me!" And Joseph does the wisest thing possible: he leaves his cloak behind and runs.

There is deep wisdom in Joseph's flight. He did not stay to argue, to reason, or to test his own willpower. He did not think, "I'm strong enough to resist even here." He ran. When temptation had him by the cloak, Joseph would rather lose the cloak than lose his integrity.

This is exactly what the New Testament tells us to do. "Flee from sexual immorality" (1 Cor 6:18). "Flee the evil desires of youth" (2 Tim 2:22). Some temptations are not to be reasoned with or bravely faced — they are to be fled. There is no shame in running from sin; it is courage, not cowardice. The hero here is the one who flees.

Notice, too, that fleeing cost Joseph something. He lost his cloak, and that very cloak would soon be used against him. Doing the right thing sometimes leaves us exposed and gives our accusers something to hold. But it is always better to flee sin and pay a price than to stay and fall. When temptation grabs you by the cloak, run.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I flee temptation, or stay and test my willpower?
2. Where do I need to simply run rather than reason with sin?
3. Am I willing to pay a price to keep my integrity?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, give me the wisdom and courage to flee from sin rather than to toy with it. When temptation grabs me, help me to run, willing to pay any price to keep my integrity before You. Amen.
